test_title: PYST 68: RRB Group D - GS (Held On: 27 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: An object is placed at a distance of 40 cm from a convex lens of focal length 10 cm, such that an image is formed at a distance of X cm from the lens. What is the value of X?
solution:
The correct answer is __**+40/3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To find the image distance in a lens system, we use the **Lens Formula**, which is given by: **1/f = 1/v - 1/u**.
 
• In this problem, the object is placed at a **distance of 40 cm** from the lens. According to the **Cartesian sign convention**, the object distance (**u**) is always taken as **negative**. Therefore, **u = -40 cm**.
 
• The lens provided is a **convex lens** with a **focal length (f) of 10 cm**. For a convex lens, the focal length is always considered **positive**. Thus, **f = +10 cm**.
 
• Substituting these values into the lens formula:
 
 
• **1/10 = 1/v - 1/(-40)**
 
• **1/10 = 1/v + 1/40**
 
 
 
• Rearranging the equation to solve for **1/v**:
 
 
• **1/v = 1/10 - 1/40**
 
• Taking the **LCM** of 10 and 40, which is **40**:
 
• **1/v = (4 - 1) / 40**
 
• **1/v = 3 / 40**
 
 
 
• Therefore, **v = 40/3 cm**. Since the value is positive, the image is formed on the **opposite side** of the lens. ***Hence, the correct answer is +40/3.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Convex Lens:** Also known as a **converging lens**, it is thicker at the center than at the edges. It converges parallel rays of light to a point called the **principal focus**. It is used in **microscopes**, **telescopes**, and for correcting **hypermetropia** (long-sightedness).
 
• **Sign Convention for Lenses:** 
 
 
• The **optical center** is treated as the origin.
 
• Distances measured in the direction of **incident light** are positive, while those measured against it are negative.
 
• The **object** is always placed on the **left** side of the lens, making **u** negative.
 
• For a **convex lens**, **f** is **positive**; for a **concave lens**, **f** is **negative**.
 
 
 
• **Nature of Image:** In this specific case, since **v** is positive, the image is **real and inverted**. Because the absolute value of **v** (approx 13.33 cm) is less than the absolute value of **u** (40 cm), the image is **diminished**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Magnification (m):** It is the ratio of the height of the image to the height of the object, also expressed as **m = v/u** for lenses. 
 
 
• In this problem, **m = (40/3) / (-40) = -1/3**.
 
• The **negative sign** indicates that the image is **inverted**, and the value **1/3** indicates that the image is **one-third** the size of the object.
 
 
 
• **Power of Lens:** The reciprocal of the focal length in meters is called **Power (P)**. **P = 1/f (in meters)**. The **SI unit** is **Dioptre (D)**. For this lens, **f = 0.1 m**, so **P = +10 D**.
 
• **Focal Length Comparison:** If the object is placed beyond **2f** (which is 20 cm in this case), the image always forms between **f and 2f** on the other side. Here, **u = 40 cm** (which is > 20 cm), and **v = 13.33 cm** (which is between 10 cm and 20 cm), confirming the laws of **refraction**.
